editorNote: Today's picks lean on small, fast models: OpenAI and an open-source project both ship decision models, Google shrinks embeddings, and Chrome finally ships JPEG XL, written in Rust. An AI-designed accelerator on a decade-old FPGA rounds out the list.

stories.headline: OpenAI puts a Decisions API into public beta: typed answers about 10x faster than Responses, at $0.10 per million input tokens
stories.summary: The endpoint returns predicates, choices or scores for text and images, currently only on gpt-6-luna. General availability is promised in the coming weeks.
stories.whyItMatters: Classification and routing get a dedicated, cheaper endpoint rather than free-form text generation.

stories.headline: Chrome 155 ships JPEG XL, decoded by a Rust implementation
stories.summary: Google says the jxl-rs decoder, claimed to offer 30–50% better compression than JPEG, has had zero memory-safety bugs in development. The team cites developer demand through the Interop Project.
stories.whyItMatters: A format Chrome had resisted is now supported, and with a memory-safe decoder.

stories.headline: Strands releases Decider 2B, an open-source decision model that runs locally
stories.summary: Built on Qwen 3.5-2B with the language head replaced by a pointer head, it picks among predefined options, with median latency of about 115 ms on an RTX 3090. It ranks 3rd of 33 in the 2B class on JevBench; training data and scripts are published.
stories.whyItMatters: Routing and guardrail decisions can run on a laptop instead of an API call.

stories.headline: Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, images, audio and video into one embedding space
stories.summary: The 740M-parameter Apache 2.0 model needs about 191MB of RAM for text-only use and 567MB for the full multimodal version, and compresses vectors from 768 to 128 dimensions.
stories.whyItMatters: A sub-1B multimodal embedder that fits on a phone lowers the cost of on-device search.

stories.headline: OpenTPU: an open-source accelerator designed by AI agents runs Qwen3 on an old Kintex-7 FPGA
stories.summary: The repo bundles RTL, ISA, simulator, compiler and profiler; the four-column systolic design runs at 133.33 MHz and reaches 82–94% of DDR3 peak bandwidth in decoding.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a concrete data point on agent-driven hardware design, modest in speed but fully inspectable.

stories.headline: A blog post explains 'codemode': letting the model run JavaScript inside the agent harness
stories.summary: The post shows codemode orchestrating concurrent work, persisting state and calling MCP servers, while noting MCP's lack of structured returns and weak tool discovery.
stories.whyItMatters: It frames a design choice for agent builders: compose work in code rather than one tool call at a time.
